flavour.text: Earthy, with areca-nut and dried-wood notes in aged leaf; smooth and gentle on the palate.

history.text: Liubao tea is grown and pressed in the hills around Liubao town of Cangwu county, Wuzhou. It was shipped from the Qing to Southeast Asian tin miners through Hong Kong, giving it a historic overseas-trade market. The Liubao tradition was listed as national intangible heritage in 2014.

harvest.text: Spring to summer; mature leaves, pile-fermented after rolling and sun-drying.

brewing.text: 95–100 °C, 5 g per 150 ml, rinse first, 8–12 infusions.

teas.place: 南平市政和县

location.text: 南平市政和县 · 福建

flavour.text: Longer, straighter needles than Fuding's; delicate hay and dried-pear notes, with a thicker, almost rice-like body.

history.text: Zhenghe's Baihao Yinzhen is made from the large-bud Zhenghe Dabai cultivar; records date it to around 1880. One of Fujian's three "gongfu" historic exports is also from Zhenghe, so the county counts both the white and the black among its specialty teas.

harvest.text: Pre-Qingming to early April; single bud only.

brewing.text: 85–90 °C, 4 g per 150 ml, 40 s first steep, 4–5 infusions.

teas.place: 黄山市祁门县

location.text: 黄山市祁门县 · 安徽

flavour.text: Honey and orchid notes, a cocoa-and-rose "Qimen fragrance", a smooth cup with a long sweet finish.

history.text: Qimen Hongcha (Keemun) was first made in 1875 in Qimen county, Anhui, based on the gongfu black-tea methods brought from Fujian. It is grouped with Darjeeling and Uva as one of the world's three great fragrant black teas. Qimen gongfu was listed as intangible heritage in 2008.

harvest.text: Spring, standard bud with two leaves; summer pickings also used.

brewing.text: 90–95 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 15 s first steep, 4–5 infusions.

teas.place: 黄山市歙县

location.text: 黄山市歙县 · 安徽

flavour.text: A smoky, nutty character from heavy pan-firing; thick body and long chestnut-sweet aftertaste.

history.text: Lao Zhu Dafang is one of the ancestors of Longjing's flat-leaf pan-firing style, and was produced in Shexian under the Ming. It is the main source cultivar for scented Zhulan Dafang jasmine tea.

harvest.text: Pre-Qingming to Guyu; one bud and two or three leaves.

brewing.text: 80–85 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 30 s first steep, 3 infusions.

flavour.text: Honey, lychee, with a long sugar-like finish and a bright, clear liquor.

history.text: Lichuan Hong was made famous after 2018 by its service as a diplomatic gift at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Qingdao. It is black tea from the Qingmaoyuan plateau of Lichuan.

harvest.text: Spring picking.

brewing.text: 90–95 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 15 s first steep, 4–5 infusions.

flavour.text: Deep sweet-corn aroma, buttery mouthfeel, lightly honeyed finish and a bright yellow liquor.

history.text: Yuan'an Luyuan is a Southern Song-era yellow tea developed at Luyuan temple, with records dating to the 1225 Jiading reign. The manufacturing technique was listed as national intangible heritage in 2014.

harvest.text: Pre-Guyu; one bud and one leaf.

brewing.text: 80–85 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 30 s first steep, 3–4 infusions.

location.text: 益阳市安化县 · 湖南

flavour.text: Rich sweet-earth notes with the characteristic "golden flower" mushroom fragrance; thick, smooth body.

history.text: Anhua Fuzhuan has been pressed in Anhua as a successor to Jingyang fuzhuan since 1953, with the "jin hua" (golden flower) Eurotium cristatum colony developed under the brick's controlled fungal step. Listed as intangible heritage in 2008.

harvest.text: Summer to autumn; mature leaves.

brewing.text: 95–100 °C, 5 g per 150 ml, rinse first, 6–8 infusions.

teas.place: 咸阳市泾阳县

location.text: 咸阳市泾阳县 · 陕西

flavour.text: Nutty mushroom-earth notes with a dry, warming finish; cleaner and lighter than Anhua's Fuzhuan.

history.text: Jingyang fuzhuan has been pressed in the Guanzhong basin since the Northern Song. The manufacturing technique was listed as national intangible heritage in 2008, and the Jingyang climate is said to allow the Eurotium cristatum "golden flower" to bloom reliably in the brick.

harvest.text: Processed from Anhua black-tea maocha shipped to Jingyang for fermentation and pressing.

brewing.text: 95–100 °C, 5 g per 150 ml, rinse first, 6–8 infusions.

teas.place: 临沧市凤庆县

location.text: 临沧市凤庆县 · 云南

flavour.text: Honey, cocoa and sweet potato, a thick golden-tipped liquor and a long sweet finish.

history.text: Dianhong gongfu black tea was created in 1938 by Feng Shaoqiu at Fengqing's Shunning tea factory, repurposing Yunnan large-leaf stock from brick-tea to export black tea. Manufacturing listed as intangible heritage in 2014.

harvest.text: Spring to autumn; Yunnan large-leaf stock, standard bud with one or two leaves.

brewing.text: 90–95 °C, 4 g per 150 ml, 15 s first steep, 4–5 infusions.

location.text: 宜宾市 · 四川

flavour.text: Sweet-potato, cocoa and orchid notes; smooth, golden-tipped and bright.

harvest.text: Spring; standard bud with two leaves from the Yibin early-cultivar belt.

brewing.text: 90–95 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 15 s first steep, 4–5 infusions.

harvest.text: Pre-Qingming; single bud only, pan-fired into a tongue-flat shape.

brewing.text: 80–85 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 30 s first steep, 3 infusions.

harvest.text: Pre-Qingming; one bud and one leaf.

brewing.text: 80–85 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 30 s first steep, 3–4 infusions.

harvest.text: Pre-Qingming; one bud and one leaf.

brewing.text: 80–85 °C, 3 g per 150 ml, 30 s first steep, 3–4 infusions.

wuyi.text: Wuyi rock tea method: boiling water in a gaiwan or clay pot, roughly half filled with dry leaves by volume; a quick rinse, then 5–10 seconds. After the third infusion, add about 5 seconds per steep. Adjust for the actual leaf and vessel.

red.text: Cup-style black tea method: water above 90°C; steep 2–5 minutes depending on leaf size. The article does not give a leaf-to-water ratio. This is category guidance, not a tested recipe for every named tea.

yellow.text: Category guidance: 85–90°C water; first infusion 30 seconds, second 60 seconds, third about 2 minutes. The source specifies dry leaves occupying roughly one quarter of the vessel by volume.
